ownership: Independent bounded producer review of existing IDEA000926. No native forms or meanings, source counts, decoder, new corpus or changes to the parent experiment.

source_positive.source: Cappelli, The elements of abbreviation in medieval Latin paleography, Heimann/Kay translation, 1982, printed pages 33 and 35, sections 5.45 and 5.62.
source_positive.inspection: The two already cached printed page images were visually re-read in this block. These are handbook reproductions, not a newly collated original manuscript or independent confirmation.
source_positive.narrow_rule: The printed joint head-plus-attached-letter forms have finite licensed expansions: h with superscript oo expands to hoc modo; h with on to hoc nomen; the marked ut head with t to ut dicit and with r to ut probatur. The page image owns every mark and position; these verbal descriptions are not normalized strings.
source_positive.useful_ladder: The top of page 35 also prints h with superscript o for hoc. It is therefore possible to see a specific known head participating in both a one-word and a two-word construction. This does not license the second o as a general independently meaningful modo operator.
source_positive.countercase: Section 5.45 gives raised ordinary final s in patris, with a twelfth-century qualification. Elevation alone therefore determines neither omission nor following-word scope.

manual_generalization_check.proposed_but_unlicensed_generalization: Retain the known first-word head and append the last letter of any following word above it.
manual_generalization_check.content_contrast: Read this name versus read this volume. Both are grammatical illustrative instructions; they are not historical source quotations.
manual_generalization_check.collision: Both following nouns end in n and both have the same hoc head. The proposed generalized last-letter rule therefore yields the same compressed first pair, followed by the same lege, while the instructions retain different objects.
manual_generalization_check.scope: This rejects the proposed unrestricted exact-recovery generalization, not Cappelli's four licensed forms and not contextual reading in general. A declared ambiguous note may preserve less information, but it cannot claim the two instructions remain distinguishable without a paid additional condition.

complete_writer_boundary.available_hand_step: Learn the four whole head-plus-mark expansions and use only their printed licenses. Their ordinary reading is concrete source evidence.
complete_writer_boundary.not_yet_supplied: A full writer would additionally need an explicit ordinary writing channel for everything else, separation between literal superscripts and abbreviation forms, a collision policy, open names and unknown words, word and sentence boundaries, and physical continuation. No such complete 22-working-sign channel follows from these four pairs.
complete_writer_boundary.cost: At least four learned phrase-to-form licenses, the distinct literal-final-letter convention, and the normal source language vocabulary and grammar are paid. Recognizing a characteristic letter does not remove the lexical association cost.
complete_writer_boundary.why_no_new_card: A four-phrase macro table plus ordinary full spelling would be a finite conventional shortcut system. Generic multiword shorthand is already retained in IDEA131 and heterogeneous abbreviation in GDT609. Merely adding those familiar fallback obligations would not establish a genuinely new productive shared writing rule or a decision-changing new test.

prior_and_followup_limits.scope: The frozen 44-right/7-left German spelling lists and four cached recipe projections failed their necessary frequency comparison. They did not execute these four Latin phrase abbreviations.
Its fixed dependency-relation grouping of adjacent ITTB words failed its type bounds. This is not a universal exclusion of historical two-word abbreviation or a run of the four Cappelli pairs.

The old four-source one-word-to-one-group contract with at most two surface forms does not apply unchanged when one printed group expands into two lexical words. This logical difference alone supplies neither adequate source coverage nor a selected replacement writer.
IDEA131 already preserves compact multiword notes and a positional contrast. Multiple source words per written construction is not a new discovery.
Contextual word restoration and non-preservation of some endings are already retained; the failed source-control and missing complete-channel decisions are not reopened by these examples.

Heterogeneous outputs and paid whole forms are existing architecture. Lookup followups 612/613/614 and the original strict GDT616 failure remain; four historical pairs do not validate the old numerical capacities.
The primary original decision is NO_JOINT_CHILD_FEASIBLE_BINDING. Its later diagnostic relaxation is not a reopening or a successful unknown-key writer.
The fixed source-control pipeline remains failed. No vocabulary, threshold, omission-search or decoder repair is proposed.

retrieval_scope: Live route and composition topic, bounded card/search/duplicates/route-check, targeted lookup followups and the claim-bearing primaries. Absence of an additional exact full-channel run in this bounded review is not an exhaustive proof of absent research.
disposition: Retain IDEA000926 as the existing raw finite source relation. No new proposal, experiment or general historical writing law is selected. The exact remaining constructive problem is a paid open-word disambiguation and fallback channel; its need is demonstrated by the explicit last-letter collision, not inferred merely from missing metadata.
